en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: This course provides students with a basic understanding of analytical chemistry. The aim of the course is to introduce students to chemical and instrumental analytical methods. The laboratory exercises focus primarily on the application of instrumental methods in analysis.

en.label: [section] Course content:
en.content: 1.Basic chemical calculations (allowance 4/0) a.Titration stoichiometry.b.Calculations of pH of solutions.c.Titration curves, evaluation of titration curves.2.Quantitative analysis (allowance 2/0) a.Sampling of gaseous, liquid and solid samples.b.Dry and wet sample digestion, concentration.3.Chemical equilibrium (allowance 4/0) a.Acid-base equilibria, acidimetry, alkalimetry.b.Complexation equilibria, chelatometry.c.Oxidation-reduction equilibria, manganometry, iodometry.4.Optical methods (allowance 6/0) a.Refractometry and polarimetry.b.Atomic absorption spectrometry, molecular absorption spectrometry.c.Infrared spectrometry.d.Atomic emission spectrometry.e.Photoluminescence methods.5.Electrochemical methods (allowance 6/0) a.Types of electrodes, direct potentiometry and potentiometric titrations.b.Conductometry, direct and conductometric titrations.c.Polarography.d.Electrogravimetry.6.Separation methods (allowance 4/0) a.Extraction. Ion exchangers.b.Liquid chromatography, column chromatography.c.Gas chromatography. Evaluation of chromatograms.7.Electromigration methods (allowance 2/0) a.Electrophoresis and isotachophoresis.8.Practical laboratory exercises (allowance 0/42) a.Measurement analysis: chelatometry, alkalimetry, acidimetry, manganometry, iodometry.b.Optical methods: molecular absorption spectrometry, refractometry.c.Electrochemical methods: potentiometry, conductometry.
